newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee untraded on lack of import demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee untraded on lack of import demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was untraded nearly three hours after the market opened because of a lack of demand and speculation, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 57.26, after opening at its previous closing level of 57.25, they said.

"There is no import covering to compel buying. Since indications from the Central Bank are that they are keen to keep rates low, there is no incentive to create positions either," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The Central Bank left the exchange rate unchanged. Buying and selling prices remained at 56.2122 and 57.3478
With the upside limited by the Central Bank's top level, which is just a few cents away, and the downside unlimited, there is no incentive to build positions, dealers said.
Overnight call money rose early to 15 percent, but fell back to 14, dealers said.
"The initial rise in call rates was caused by panic, when banks found investors buying Treasury Bills in the secondary market due to falling primary market rates," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
